item.title: One Pair Across Every Shot

turns.text: Make a realistic, silent 15-second widescreen story in three shots: a woman with a freckled face and red pixie cut drops a red scarf; a man with a shaved head and round glasses picks it up; he returns it and they smile. Both adults, on a quiet street. Show both faces clearly in every shot and keep exactly the same two faces throughout—no changing actors between cuts.

item.tests: Maintains two distinct generated facial identities across three story shots, including shots where either character is the focus.

answer_sheet.Character identities: An adult woman with a freckled face and red pixie cut, and an adult man with a shaved head and round glasses. Invent their faces but keep each identity unchanged across all three shots.
answer_sheet.Face visibility: Both faces must be clearly visible in every shot, including when the scarf is dropped and picked up.
answer_sheet.Story and setting: On a quiet street, the woman drops a red scarf, the man picks it up, and he returns it before they smile at each other.
answer_sheet.Length and format: One 15-second widescreen 16:9 video in three shots.
answer_sheet.Style and mood: Realistic live action, a small friendly encounter.
answer_sheet.Sound and text: Silent, with no captions, titles or dialogue.

must_haves: One assembled 15-second 16:9 film tells the story in three distinct shots.
The woman retains the same facial structure, freckles and red pixie cut in all three shots.
The man retains the same facial structure, shaved head and round glasses in all three shots; the two identities never merge or swap.
Both faces are clearly visible in every shot, not hidden by rear views, distant framing or object-only cutaways.
The red scarf is dropped by the woman, picked up by the man and returned to her in that order, ending with mutual smiles.
The film looks realistic and has no audible soundtrack.

I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what this will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter or smaller way to do it?
turns.agent:
**I haven’t started any generation or spent any credits.**

Your story can be attempted, but **exactly identical faces across three cuts cannot be guaranteed**. Keeping both adults’ faces visible in every shot also calls for medium two-shots rather than close-ups of the scarf.

### Cost and free-plan limits
- Your free-plan video options are **LTX 2.5 or MiniMax H3 at 480p**. Widescreen **16:9** and silent output can be requested.
- I don’t have an account-balance or live video-price tool available here, so **I can’t give you a reliable credit total or confirm that a 15-second job is eligible and affordable**. I won’t submit a generation to discover the price.
- A generated reference image of the pair would add a separate cost; free-plan image generation starts at **5 credits for one 640px image**, depending on the model.

### Best approach for your story
First approve a reference image showing both adults clearly. Then use it to anchor a single video with three planned shots:
1. She drops the red scarf, with him nearby.
2. He picks it up while she remains in frame.
3. He returns it; they smile.

That reference should help continuity, but it is **not an identity lock**, especially across cuts.

### Cheaper alternatives
| Option | Trade-off |
|---|---|
| **Shorter, 6–9 seconds, three shots** | Likely lower cost, but the actions may feel rushed and cuts still risk face changes. |
| **5 seconds, one continuous two-shot** | A more economical first test, with less identity drift; simplifies your three-shot requirement. |
| **480p instead of higher resolution** | Already the available free-plan size; I can’t offer a smaller supported video setting. |

**My recommendation:** check the displayed price and duration eligibility in [Magic Hour’s video generator](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-video-generator) before authorizing anything. If unchanged faces are non-negotiable, I would not spend credits on AI-generated cuts expecting a guarantee.
